description: Three-phase multimeter and transducer family: voltages, currents, frequency, power, power factor, energy, demand, THD, minimums and maximums, settings and reset commands
notes: Modbus RTU on RS-485. Addresses are numbered from 1 as in the document (30.015 is input register 15, sent as 14; 40.001 is holding register 1). Commands are coils: command 006 is coil 6, sent as 5.

Float values use the KRON sequence F2, F1, F0, EXP, which is the bytes fully reversed (the document's example sends 60 Hz as 00 00 70 42): little byte order and little word order. That is the default of holding register 301; changing it breaks the float registers. Integer registers (MSB, LSB) override this with big byte order.

The document lists the models Mult-K, Mult-K Plus, Mult-K Grafic, Mult-K C, Mult-K 05 and Mult-K 120. Some registers exist only on some of them; this is said in the description of each register. The document does not say whether the registers are absent or return an error on the others.
Holding registers are read at most 12 at a time and written at most 10; input registers up to 94 at a time. The max_read_registers value of 12 is the smaller limit.

Serial settings: 9600 to 57600 bit/s, 8 data bits, parity none, even or odd, 1 or 2 stop bits. The document gives no factory default; 9600 8N1 and address 1 are assumed here. The baud rate and format fields are available on Mult-K 05, Mult-K 120 and Mult-K 30Wh through holding register 7; the other models are set on the display.

The document also describes unsigned and signed 16-bit copies of the readings (registers 38.301 to 38.762). They are scaled by model, TP and TC with formulas in the document and are not mapped. The minimums and maximums are listed for Mult-K Grafic and Mult-K C; the document marks some of them as also available on Mult-K Plus from firmware 3.0. The special functions (0x42 Config Address, 0x71, 0x75, 0x76) and Report Slave ID, whose answer is not the standard layout, are not mapped.
Written from the protocol document; this map has not been tested on a device.

registers.name: Floating point byte sequence
registers.description: Order of the four bytes of a float. The high byte is the position of the first byte sent, the low byte the second, and so on over the two registers; 0x3210 (F2, F1, F0, EXP) is the KRON default this map assumes. Changing it breaks the float registers. Not available on special versions (for example Mult-K Plus E-10 and E-13)
